name: Route planning
summary: Takes the day's stops from the business's dispatch platform, finds the stops not yet in a route, and queues a dispatch of each team's routes for approval. Crons read and draft; a person approves every dispatch that sends a driver out.

covered_by.gather-stops: intake (stops held in the store, no address flagged)
covered_by.check-capacity: skill (team and worker limits are set in Onfleet, not read here)
covered_by.build-routes: plan (counts unrouted stops per team, queues dispatch)
covered_by.optimise-sequence: plan (Onfleet auto-dispatch orders the stops; scheduled optimisation not wired)
covered_by.customer-notify: not changed here (Onfleet's own notification settings)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: Reads tasks from the dispatch platform since the last run and keeps them as stops. Flags stops with no address.

crons.name: plan
crons.summary: Counts stops not yet in a route for each team. Drafts a plan note and queues one team dispatch per day for approval.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations are reads only: tasks and route plans. Nothing a cron drafts reaches a driver or a customer. A team dispatch sends routes to drivers, so it is a live operation and waits for a person.

onfleet.covers: task list, route plans, team auto-dispatch (Scale plan or higher per the Onfleet docs)

gaps: Confirm the workflow steps and platform coverage with the business before enabling its crons.
Locate2u: the route planning and driver app are documented on marketing and training pages, but the kit has no ops file for it, so no adapter is built.
Webfleet: its pages are vehicle tracking marketing, not route planning or dispatch documentation, and the kit has no ops file for it. No adapter is built.
Onfleet auto-dispatch is a Scale plan feature per its docs. A business on a lower plan cannot run the dispatch step until it upgrades or uses another route.
Onfleet scheduled route optimisation (optimizations/scheduled) is mapped in the kit but not wired: its request body is not confirmed from the docs read here.
Creating tasks for new stops (tasks, taskOrders) is not wired. Stops are expected to arrive in Onfleet from the business's own system or the Onfleet dashboard.
Mid-day changes, failed-delivery follow-up and cancellations are not wired. The state codes for failed and completed tasks are not confirmed from the docs read here.
Mass, height, access, curfew and work diary checks are not in the Onfleet docs read here. Check them with the business before dispatch.
Customer notifications go out from Onfleet's own settings. This workflow does not change them, and the approval summary does not show them.
The Onfleet support host returned no pages, so the Onfleet steps rest on its marketing pages and the API reference, not on how-to guides.
Onfleet metadata queries (workers, teams, tasks metadata) are POST reads that the kit marks as writes, so they are not used by the crons.
Every adapter is docs-only until a sandbox account proves it. The offline test covers the workflow's rules, not a real Onfleet account.
settings_note: settings.example.json names the team ids and where each route ends. The team ids must be set per client.
